label: token b fed back as the first or second copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input is b and that b is the first or second copied token, i.e. orig(0) or orig(1) == b being fed back (recall_idx 1 or 2). Magnitude is much larger at recall_idx 1, where b is the first original token and the step right after <DEL> (about 0.8-1.0 of max; 83% of activation mass). At recall_idx 2, where b was the second original token, it is weak (about 0.02-0.3 of max). Never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter, on b at later copy positions, or on other tokens. Most false positives are short sequences (L=3-4) with b in position 1, where the activation drops to zero; misses are tiny activations of about 0.01.

issues: The core claims hold. Activity is copy-phase only (orig/delimiter share 0). in_tok b carries 100% of the activation mass, and recall_idx 1 and 2 carry 83.5% and 16.5% of it. recall_idx 2 activations sit only in the bottom two activation quartiles, which matches 'weak'. b & recall_idx==1 has dev precision 1.0.

There is a systematic false-positive class tied to sequence length, and the predicate does not encode it. For b & recall_idx==2: L=3 has test precision 0.002 (essentially never fires); L=4 has test precision 0.41; L>=5 has dev precision 0.998. Nearly all of the ~1855 test false positives are L=3/4 sequences with b in position 1, e.g. '3 b x d <DEL> 3 *b*'. The explanation mentions this, but the label and predicate leave it out, so the label overclaims for 'second copied token'.
The misses (33 on test) are scattered tiny activations of 0.01-0.10 holding 0.0% of the mass. This is noise and not a systematic gap.
Adding L>=5 to the recall_idx==2 branch raises test precision from 0.944 to 0.999 and F1 from 0.971 to 0.983, with mass recall 0.997. Using L>=4 instead gives F1 0.977.
skeptic.revised_label: token b fed back as the first copied token (strong), or weakly as the second copied token in longer sequences (L>=5)

final_label: token b fed back as the first copied token (strong), or weakly as the second copied token in longer sequences (L>=5)
